pages.text: Taro sat on the porch holding a whole bunch of bananas. Mom wiped leaf plates nearby. "Dinner will be ready soon." "Just one more, one more!" Peels piled up beside him.
The peel pile grew as high as Taro's knees. He gobbled the last banana. His belly bulged, and even his hands moved slowly.
Mumu called from the well tree. "Let's hop across stream stones!" Taro stood and wobbled, his belly heavy. At the first stone, he stopped.
"My tummy's too full to jump." Taro plopped onto a stone. Mumu bounded across three stones and came back. "Even your hands are slow today."
Dinner was ready on Taro's porch. Beside the peel pile, rice and fish sat untouched. "I can't eat rice. There's no room."
Mumu made a small circle with both hands. "Your tummy is a little container. Fill it with bananas, and rice can't fit. Leave the rest of the space for your meal."
The next afternoon, Taro ate just two bananas and stopped. He wrapped the rest in a leaf and set them at the porch's edge. He held up two fingers. "Only Two Bananas!"
At dinner, his tummy rumbled. Taro finished all the rice and fish. "Was rice always this good?" With the last bite, he tapped twice with his branch. Tok-tok.
Now Taro knew how to count bananas. "One, only two bananas! Two, meals come first! Three, wrap the rest in a leaf!" At the stream, he hopped across five stepping stones.
Mumu held and shook Taro's hand. "You crossed five stones today!" A small snack left meals tasty and his body light. Taro pointed to the stream. "Let's hop again tomorrow! Only Two Bananas!"
